questions.text: Which of the following statements about the text is FALSE?
options: The Himalayas grow about 5 millimeters annually
The Indian plate collides with the Eurasian plate
The mountain-building process is called orogeny
India moved northward at a rate of 25 centimeters per year
The collision began approximately 50 million years ago
questions.correctAnswer: India moved northward at a rate of 25 centimeters per year
questions.explanation: Text 1 states that India moved northward at a rate of 15 centimeters per year, not 25.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the text is FALSE?
options: The Himalayas contain over 30 peaks exceeding 7,500 meters
Compression forces push sedimentary rock upward
Permanent snow and ice exist above 5,500 meters
The ecological gradient includes tropical forests
The International Mountain Research Institute is located in Nepal
questions.correctAnswer: The International Mountain Research Institute is located in Nepal
questions.explanation: The text mentions geologists from the International Mountain Research Institute, but does not state its location is in Nepal.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the text is FALSE?
options: Quantum computers use qubits instead of traditional bits
Qubits can exist in multiple states simultaneously
Quantum computers can currently solve all problems faster than classical computers
Quantum decoherence involves the loss of quantum information
Quantum computing leverages phenomena like superposition
questions.correctAnswer: Quantum computers can currently solve all problems faster than classical computers
questions.explanation: Text 2 states that quantum computers can solve certain problems exponentially faster, not all problems.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the text is FALSE?
options: Quantum systems require cooling to near absolute zero
IBM and Google have achieved quantum advantage for specific problems
Practical quantum computers are available for commercial use today
The temperature near absolute zero is approximately -273.15°C
Quantum entanglement is mentioned as a quantum mechanical phenomenon
questions.correctAnswer: Practical quantum computers are available for commercial use today
questions.explanation: Text 2 states that practical, error-corrected quantum computers remain years away.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the text is FALSE?
options: Sucrose is composed of glucose and fructose
The enzyme sucrase breaks down sucrose in the small intestine
Fructose is metabolized primarily by the kidneys
Excessive fructose can be converted to fat in the liver
The process of converting fructose to fat is called de novo lipogenesis
questions.correctAnswer: Fructose is metabolized primarily by the kidneys
questions.explanation: Text 3 states that fructose is primarily processed by the liver, not the kidneys.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the text is FALSE?
options: The WHO recommends limiting added sugar to less than 10% of daily calories
Studies have conclusively proven that sugar causes hyperactivity in children
High sugar consumption is linked to metabolic disorders
The ideal sugar consumption is below 25 grams per day
Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease is mentioned as a potential risk
questions.correctAnswer: Studies have conclusively proven that sugar causes hyperactivity in children
questions.explanation: Text 3 states that contrary to popular belief, studies have NOT conclusively demonstrated that sugar directly causes hyperactivity in children.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the text is FALSE?
options: Schizophrenia affects approximately 1% of the global population
The disorder is characterized by changes in perception and thought processes
Most effective antipsychotic medications target serotonin receptors
Brain imaging shows reduced gray matter in the prefrontal cortex
Enlarged ventricles are mentioned as a brain abnormality
questions.correctAnswer: Most effective antipsychotic medications target serotonin receptors
questions.explanation: Text 4 states that most effective antipsychotic medications function as dopamine receptor antagonists, not serotonin receptors.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the text is FALSE?
options: Modern treatment combines medication with psychosocial interventions
Second-generation antipsychotics have fewer extrapyramidal side effects
Early intervention improves long-term outcomes
Most individuals with schizophrenia are highly violent
Olanzapine and risperidone are second-generation antipsychotics
questions.correctAnswer: Most individuals with schizophrenia are highly violent
questions.explanation: Text 4 states that despite misconceptions, most individuals with schizophrenia are NOT violent.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the text is FALSE?
options: The Gulf Stream transfers heat from the Gulf of Mexico to the North Atlantic
Ocean currents are driven in part by the Coriolis effect
The global ocean conveyor belt circulates water between major ocean basins
Without the Gulf Stream, Europe would be approximately 10°C colder
The Gulf Stream moderates Europe's climate
questions.correctAnswer: Without the Gulf Stream, Europe would be approximately 10°C colder
questions.explanation: Text 5 states that without this thermal regulation, regions would experience temperatures as much as 5°C colder, not 10°C.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the text is FALSE?
options: Ocean currents distribute nutrients across oceanic regions
Salinity variations help drive ocean currents
Rising temperatures might slow the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation
The Scripps Institution of Oceanography is mentioned in the text
The text states that ocean currents have no effect on biodiversity
questions.correctAnswer: The text states that ocean currents have no effect on biodiversity
questions.explanation: Text 5 states that currents distribute nutrients and larvae, supporting biodiversity across vast oceanic regions.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the text is FALSE?
options: Black holes form primarily from collapsed cores of massive stars
Light cannot escape once it passes the event horizon
Stellar black holes typically have masses 5-100 times that of our Sun
Black holes function similarly to vacuum cleaners in space
The Milky Way contains a supermassive black hole
questions.correctAnswer: Black holes function similarly to vacuum cleaners in space
questions.explanation: Text 6 explicitly states: Black holes don't 'suck' matter like vacuum cleaners.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the text is FALSE?
options: The first direct image of a black hole was captured in 2019
Einstein's general theory of relativity predicted how light bends around black holes
Matter approaching a black hole forms an accretion disk
Accretion disks emit X-rays and other radiation
The average black hole has the exact same mass as our Sun
questions.correctAnswer: The average black hole has the exact same mass as our Sun
questions.explanation: Text 6 distinguishes stellar black holes (5-100 times the mass of our Sun) and supermassive ones (millions or billions of times), and does not state any average black hole equals the Sun's exact mass.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the text is FALSE?
options: Sugar was originally a luxury available only to the wealthy
Sugar production involved the forced migration of enslaved Africans
Sugar was first introduced to European diets in the 12th century
Sugar plantations were established throughout the Caribbean
Sugar played a role in the triangular slave trade
questions.correctAnswer: Sugar was first introduced to European diets in the 12th century
questions.explanation: Text 7 states that sugar was introduced to European diets in the 15th century, not the 12th century.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the text is FALSE?
options: Sugarcane cultivation originated in New Guinea
Sugar beet processing reduced dependence on tropical cane sugar
Brazil is mentioned as a major sugar producer
The average American consumes 71 grams of added sugar daily
Global sugar production is approximately 70 million metric tons annually

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the text is FALSE?
options: Schizophrenia has a heritability estimated between 60-80%
The disorder involves a single gene mutation
Over 100 genetic loci are associated with schizophrenia
Many genes involved relate to immune function
Schizophrenia has a complex polygenic inheritance pattern
questions.correctAnswer: The disorder involves a single gene mutation
questions.explanation: The text states that unlike single-gene disorders, schizophrenia involves complex polygenic inheritance patterns.
